svg.title: Strain-wave and cycloidal reducers: follow the moving parts
svg.desc: Two original end-view schematics. In the top panel an elliptical wave generator deforms a 200-tooth flexspline into two opposite engagement regions inside a fixed 202-tooth circular spline, giving a negative one-hundredth output speed. In the bottom panel an eccentric drives a ten-lobe disc around eleven fixed outer pins. Six concentric output pins engage enlarged holes to extract the disc's slow rotation. The bottom diagram shows one disc and omits the second disc and supporting bearings. These are explanatory shapes, not manufacturing profiles or an RV gearbox drawing.
svg.text: Two ways to turn a small geometric difference into reduction
End views, simplified. Trace the input, then the output; they do not move together.
Strain-wave gearing / commonly called a harmonic drive
Output attaches to the cup’s diaphragm.
These travel with the elliptical shape.
Fixed in the housing; contact the lobes.
Disc center orbits the main shaft axis.
Orbits quickly and turns back slowly.
6 output pins on a common flange
Flange outline shown dashed, behind disc.
Profiles are explanatory. Commercial RV drives add a first stage and different support details.
